subject: Oceanography
title: Heat Transport by Currents
description: A 60-second lesson on Heat Transport by Currents.

hook.text: Ocean currents carry more heat from the tropics to the poles than all the winds in the atmosphere combined.

buildup.text: Warm surface currents flow poleward—cold deep currents return toward the equator—redistributing heat.

discovery.text: The Gulf Stream alone carries 1.4 petawatts of heat north—100 times global electricity use.

twist.text: Without ocean heat transport, the tropics would be hotter and Europe would be much colder.

climax.text: Changes in these currents reshape weather patterns—droughts, floods, and seasons across continents.

punchline.text: The ocean is Earth's central heating system—currents are the pipes.

quiz.question: How does the Gulf Stream affect Europe's climate?
options: It carries warm water north, keeping Europe mild
